title: Evaluation of the inverse compact-support restriction comparison
statement: Let f:X→Y be a scheme morphism, c a compactification, l a natural number and t:Theory(c,l) a normalized ordinary system presentation [def-pur-etale-system-projection-data]. Let B,C be finite l-power-torsion coefficient sequences, a:B→C a compatible coefficient map, and n a level. Let d be any natural isomorphism from single-ring compact support with C_n coefficients followed by restriction to B_n to restriction on X followed by B_n compact support, whose forward map is the specified singleRestriction(a_n,c). For every derived strict C-system N on X, evaluating the inverse system restriction comparison and transporting via the support/evaluation and restriction/evaluation isomorphisms gives the inverse of d. Precisely, the three-factor word supportEvaluation(B,n)^{-1} at Res_a N, then evaluation of RestrictionSupport(a)^{-1} at N, then ScalarEvaluationY(a,n).restriction at F_C N equals F_{B_n} applied to ScalarEvaluationX(a,n).restriction at N, then d^{-1} at e_n N, then single-ring restriction applied to supportEvaluation(C,n)^{-1} at N. This assertion involves restriction alone, with no scalar extension projection, scalar unit or compactScalarMap.

proof.text: At the middle scheme c.Z construct the ordinary scalar restriction/evaluation isomorphism by the identity on underlying section groups. Naturality of the constant-ring map proves linearity; the identical section map is its inverse. Exact localization provides its derived comparison, without choosing a scalar extension at c.Z. The given ordinary restriction/direct-image and restriction/evaluation comparisons are identity on every section. Extensionality of module-sheaf morphisms therefore proves the ordinary cube. Take geometric inverse-image mates: uniqueness under the ordinary adjunction Hom bijections gives the inverse-image cube. Use the actual ordinary scalar restriction comparison, not an arbitrary isomorphism between endpoints.

Apply exact-functor localization to the inverse-image cube, using the termwise normalization fields of RestrictionImage, ImageEvaluation and ScalarEvaluation. Take right geometric mates. The cube-of-mates identity identifies the proper face with scalarRestrictionDirectImageMap, including transport from exact derived inverse image to the published left-derived inverse image. This uses the canonical upperStar comparison and its adjunction-unit normalization.

For the open factor take the open-adjunction mate of the ordinary inverse-image cube, then localize the exact functors. The mate-unit equation identifies the single-ring face with derivedRestrictScalarsCompOpenImmersionLowerShriekIso. Naturality of the proper comparison pastes the proper and open cubes; their single-ring composite is singleRestriction by definition. Substitute hd and cancel the invertible evaluation, restriction and d components to get the stated inverse cube on every N. These are equalities of localized transformations; no inference from jointly faithful derived evaluation is used.

theorem etaleSystemRestriction_evaluation
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} (c : Compactification f) (l : ℕ) (t : Theory c l)
    (B C : Coefficients.{u} l) (a : B.rings ⟶ C.rings) (n : ℕ)
    (d : rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (C.rings.obj (op n))) c ⋙
        Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars Y.smallEtaleTopology (a.app (op n)).hom ≅
      Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars X.smallEtaleTopology (a.app (op n)).hom ⋙
        rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (B.rings.obj (op n))) c)
    (hd : d.hom = singleRestriction (a.app (op n)) c)
    (N : Derived X C.rings) :
    (t.supportEvaluation B n).iso.inv.app ((restriction X a).obj N) ≫
        (t.evaluationY B n).E.map ((t.restriction a).iso.inv.app N) ≫
        (t.scalarEvaluationY a n).restriction.hom.app ((t.support C).F.obj N) =
      (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (B.rings.obj (op n))) c).map
          ((t.scalarEvaluationX a n).restriction.hom.app N) ≫
        d.inv.app ((t.evaluationX C n).E.obj N) ≫
        (Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars Y.smallEtaleTopology (a.app (op n)).hom).map
          ((t.supportEvaluation C n).iso.inv.app N)
